Read off its data when omitted. An overlay, or an --animate co-animation, compares this against --canvas.

docs.title: corpus
docs.text:
corpus goes the other way from render: it reads a tidy CSV you already have and renders a styled corpus figure, as plot_corpus_figure does. For --kind profile the CSV needs word_id and value columns.

scanpath-studio corpus --input profile.csv --kind profile --output profile.svg
Option Value Default Description --input PATH required The CSV. profile reads word_id plus the value column (and optional lo / hi), distribution the value column, difference word_id and diff. --kind profile, distribution, difference required A per-word profile, a distribution, or a difference profile. -o--output PATH required Output file; any extension save_figure writes (.html, .png, .svg, .pdf). --measure-label MEASURE_LABEL Value Axis / legend label for the value (default: Value). --series-col SERIES_COL series Column naming the overlaid series, when present (default: series). --value-col VALUE_COL value The value column (default: value). --primary-color PRIMARY_COLOR #1f77b4 First series color (default: #1f77b4). --secondary-color SECONDARY_COLOR #e45756 Second series color (default: #e45756).

docs.title: check
docs.text:
check runs the Data Management page's Data checks on your tables without opening the app. It looks for:

  • fixations lasting 0 ms or less, or with an infinite duration or onset;
  • fixations and raw-gaze samples with no finite position;
  • word boxes with no area or no finite position;
  • per-screen screen sizes that are not finite and positive.

Each finding gives the rows and trials affected, a few example rows, and what the app does with them. check changes nothing and exits 0 whatever it finds. --json prints the table check_data_health returns.

scanpath-studio check --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv
scanpath-studio check --raw-gaze gaze_samples.csv --json
Option Value Default Description --sample switch — Check the bundled OneStop demo instead of your own tables. --words PATH [PATH ...] — Words table(s), as for render. --fixations PATH [PATH ...] — Fixations table(s), as for render. --raw-gaze PATH [PATH ...] — Raw (sample-level) gaze table(s), as for render. --raw-gaze-schema JSON — Column mapping for the --raw-gaze table, replacing auto-detection (same shape as --fix-schema). --trial-parts-manifest PATH — JSON manifest assigning source rows to ordered screens. --json switch — Print the findings as JSON (the rows api.check_data_health returns). --word-schema JSON — Column mapping for the --words table, replacing auto-detection: a JSON object (or a path to a .json file holding one) from each field to a column name, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}' — the same dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized; the error then prints a mapping to start from. --fix-schema JSON — Column mapping for the --fixations table, replacing auto-detection: a JSON object (or a path to a .json file holding one) from each field to a column name, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}' — the same dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized; the error then prints a mapping to start from. --keep-columns COLUMN [COLUMN ...] — Further columns of your own to carry through loading under their own names (e.g. a pupil size), from whichever table has them — otherwise loading keeps only the mapped and recognized fields. A kept fixation column can then be --color-by, an axis or a hover field. The keep_columns= of api.load_scanpath_data.

docs.title: cache
docs.text:
A local or desktop run caches your session on your own machine, so a refresh or a restart resumes where you left off: uploaded datasets, column mappings, view settings, saved designs, metadata tables and annotations. cache shows what is stored and removes it.

scanpath-studio cache            # datasets, rows, size, folder, last written
scanpath-studio cache --path     # just the folder
scanpath-studio cache --json     # the same status as JSON
scanpath-studio cache --clear    # delete the recovery cache
Option Value Default Description --path switch — Print the cache folder and exit. --json switch — Print the status as JSON. --clear switch — Delete the recovery cache.

The same information is at the foot of the Data Management page, under Saved on this computer. A running app writes a new copy at its next change, so clear the cache with the app closed.

To Use turn caching off for one launch scanpath-studio --no-persist turn it off wherever the variable is set SCANPATH_STUDIO_PERSIST=0 move the folder SCANPATH_STUDIO_STATE_DIR

Hosted deployments do not cache by default.

docs.title: version
docs.text:
version says which build this is and how it was installed. --check also asks GitHub whether a newer release is out and prints the command that updates your install. It is the only time the command uses the network.

scanpath-studio version           # the build, and how it was installed
scanpath-studio version --check   # …and whether a newer release is out
Option Value Default Description --check switch — Ask GitHub for the latest release and say how to update this install. --timeout SECONDS 5.0 How long to wait for GitHub (default 5).

Between releases the version names the build: 0.35.0.post3+g8f18219 is three commits after 0.35.0, at commit 8f18219. The same check is Help → About → Check for updates in the app, and check_for_updates in Python.

docs.title: The fixations don't line up with the text
docs.text: Words and fixations must use the same pixel coordinates and share trial IDs. If the fixations are shifted, mirrored or scaled against the words, the two tables are in different coordinate frames — a different origin, unit or offset — and no setting here fixes that; convert one of them (What your data needs → Files and units). If the alignment is right but the figure is framed or sized wrongly, the recording screen size is: set the resolution of the monitor used in the experiment under Data Management → Edit dataset → Recording setup (Screen → I know it). Estimate from my data only gives a lower bound.

docs.title: The text is too big or too small
docs.text: Text is drawn to scale from the word boxes and the recording screen size. Set the real resolution (see above); for OneStop it is 2560×1440. In Python, pass canvas_size=(2560, 1440). If it is still off, set the line spacing (how far apart the lines are, in font sizes) under Recording setup → Text size → Fit to word boxes, or line_spacing= in Python.

docs.title: A column was detected wrongly
docs.text: The app guesses columns from their names. Pick the right one under Data Management → Edit dataset, or pass word_schema / fix_schema to load_scanpath_data.

docs.title: Can I load only one table?
docs.text: Yes. A Words table alone shows the text and any reading measures it carries; a fixations table alone shows gaze positions without text. Most features need both. The same holds trial by trial: when the two tables cover different trials, every trial either one has is listed, and drawn with what it has.

docs.title: Can I open PoTeC or OneStop in the online demo?
docs.text: No. The online demo has only the bundled demo data, and it doesn't download corpora. In the desktop app or a pip install, each public corpus downloads once, with one click, and stays on your computer.

docs.title: My zip file is refused as too large
docs.text: The app limits how far a .zip may decompress (32 GB per file, 64 GB in total). The error names the setting that raises it, for example SCANPATH_ZIP_MAX_MEMBER_GB=64 scanpath-studio.

docs.title: Does the app compute reading measures?
docs.text: No. Corpus Analysis and Export show the measures your interest-area report provides, as your eye-tracking software defines them.

docs.title: Does  Filters & highlights change my data?
docs.text: No. It changes only what the figure draws. Your tables and measures stay as they are.

docs.title: Image or video export fails
docs.text: PDF, GIF and MP4 exports, static images from Python or the CLI, and image bundles need Chrome, Chromium or Edge on the computer running Scanpath Studio. Installing one is enough. With a pip install you can instead run plotly_get_chrome -y once. HTML, and the current figure's PNG and SVG, work without a browser.

docs.title: Can someone else open my share link?
docs.text: Yes, but the link does not contain your uploaded data, so they need to load the same dataset first. The bundled demo opens directly, and a public corpus opens if they have it set up.

docs.title: Where does my data go?
docs.text: When you run it locally or as the desktop app, nowhere: it stays on your computer. There are no accounts and no analytics. Don't upload identifiable data to the online demo. See Privacy.

docs.title: Will a refresh lose my work?
docs.text:
Not on a local or desktop install: the app saves your datasets and settings on this computer (when it listens only on this computer, as scanpath-studio and the desktop app do), and Data Management → Saved on this computer shows what it holds. The online demo keeps nothing, and says so after your first upload, so export your annotations and settings before you leave (what to back up).

If one saved dataset's files go missing or are damaged, the rest of the session still comes back. The app names the dataset that didn't, keeps its saved copy as it is, and offers Retry and Remove saved copy. Saved metadata tables that can't be read are kept the same way. If the whole saved copy can't be read, the app opens without it and stops saving over it until you retry or clear it.

docs.title: How do I stop saving, or delete what is saved?
docs.text: Start the app with scanpath-studio run --no-persist to save nothing. To delete what is saved and start over, use Clear what is saved… under Saved on this computer, or close the app and run scanpath-studio cache --clear. See Recovery cache.

docs.title: Where do I ask a question, report a bug or send feedback?
docs.text:
Help → Send feedback in the app lists where each kind goes — a bug report, a feature request, an idea or comment, or a question — and shows the version and system details a bug report needs, ready to copy. Nothing is sent from the app: each route is a GitHub page you submit yourself.

Ask in Discussions → Q&A. Report a bug as a GitHub issue, with the version, your operating system and how you run the app (pip, the desktop app or the online demo). Help → About shows the version and links both; on the command line, scanpath-studio --version.

docs.title: How do I update Scanpath Studio?
docs.text:
Open Help → About → Check for updates. In the desktop app, choose Update & restart. For a Python install, run:

pip install -U scanpath-studio

docs.title: Will my links, settings and scripts work after an update?
docs.text: Not necessarily. Until version 1.0, any release may change the app, its share links and saved settings, the Python API and the CLI. The changelog lists every change. To reproduce a result exactly, note the version you used and install that one: pip install scanpath-studio==<version>.

docs.title: How do I cite Scanpath Studio?
docs.text: See Cite for BibTeX and APA entries, and for the datasets you used.

docs.title: Figure options
docs.text:
Every keyword the figure builders take: the default it renders with, the render flag that sets it on the command line, and what it does. The sections follow the app's plot rail.

import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words,
    fixations,
    "l7_1090",
    "l7_1090_2_1_1_Ele_r0",
    show_heatmap=True,  # any option below, as a keyword
    heatmap_norm="log",
    fixation_color="#D55E00",
)
  • Builders. plot_scanpath, animate_scanpath and compare_scanpaths take every option, unless its description ends by naming the builders that do (Plot and compare only.). A keyword a builder does not take raises a TypeError that names the closest valid ones.
  • Fixed values. An option with a fixed set of values lists them. Case, spaces, - and _ are ignored, so the CLI's log and mark-border work; any other value raises a ValueError.
  • Descriptions are the render flag's own help. A --no-… flag describes an option that is on by default.
  • In code, figure_options() returns the same defaults, and figure_options(choices=True) adds the values.

• Desktop app Recommended

    No coding required. Your data stays on your computer.

    macOS Windows Linux

    Setup details & other downloads
    • macOS 14+, Apple silicon: open the DMG, drag to Applications, then launch. If blocked: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. Intel Mac or older macOS? Use Python below.
    • Windows: run the installer, then launch from Start. If SmartScreen warns: More info → Run anyway. A portable ZIP is also available.

    All downloads

docs.title: Your first figure
docs.text:
Start with the bundled OneStop sample. No files to prepare: choose a look and save an interactive figure.

  • 1 · Open a reading

    In Scanpath, keep Bundled demo selected. Use Select trial to choose a reading.

  • 2 · Choose a view

    Click Heatmap in Design presets to see where fixation time concentrates. Switch to Scanpath to follow the sequence.

  • 3 · Save your figure

    Open Export → Current figure, choose HTML, then download. Open the saved file to explore the figure in your browser.

docs.title: Across the experiment
docs.text:
Mean total fixation duration per word across the demo reader’s recorded trials. Each point summarizes one trial; this is the bundled subset of the session.

In the appCLIPython
  1. Select the bundled demo and open Corpus Analysis → Per participant.
  2. Choose l37_1129, Total fixation duration and Mean aggregation.
  3. Open Per-trial trend. The horizontal axis uses the dataset’s trial_index.

Follow the progression tutorial

The corpus CLI does not offer trial-order trends. Download the Python recipe and run:

python across-experiment.py

This uses the app’s aggregation and trend builder.

import scanpath_studio as sps

from scanpath_studio.aggregation import metric_by_trial_index
from scanpath_studio.data import derive_trial_index
from scanpath_studio.plots import make_trend_figure

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data(names="canonical")

reader["trial_index"] = derive_trial_index(reader)
trend = metric_by_trial_index(reader, "total_fixation_duration_ms")
fig = make_trend_figure(
    trend,
    x_col="trial_index",
    x_label="Recorded trial order",
    y_label="Mean total fixation duration per word (ms)",
    title="Across the experiment · Reader A",
    canvas_width=1000,
    base_font_size=18,
    font_family="Arial",
    height=450,

)

docs.title: Corpus Analysis
docs.text: Summarize reading measures by text, participant or group. The selected dataset and trial filters apply here too.

docs.title: Choose a view
docs.text:
View Use it to Per text Compare word-by-word reading across participants Per participant Inspect one participant across trials Groups Compare conditions or populations

Choose a measure, aggregation and spread. For word profiles, set the minimum number of participants per word.

docs.title: Supply reading measures
docs.text: Word-level analyses use the reading measures in your data, such as first fixation duration or total fixation duration. Map those columns when importing. Fixation views use the fixation table.

docs.title: Compare groups
docs.text: Split on a field or define cohorts with filters. Turn on Compare a second group to see group means and their difference. These comparisons are descriptive.

docs.title: Save results
docs.text: Download a result table as CSV and its analysis recipe as JSON. The recipe records the dataset, filters and analysis choices. Return to Scanpath to inspect individual trials.

docs.title: Plot a summary in code
docs.text:
Use a tidy summary table: a word profile needs word_id and value, with optional lo and hi for a band. Rename a source word ID column to word_id if needed. Use a result table exported from Corpus Analysis. For a trial-order trend, see Across the experiment.

Python and CLI: word profile PythonCLI 
import pandas as pd
import scanpath_studio as sps

profile = pd.read_csv("profile.csv")
fig = sps.plot_corpus_figure(
    profile, kind="profile", measure_label="Total fixation duration (ms)"
)
sps.save_figure(fig, "profile.html")

scanpath-studio corpus --input profile.csv --kind profile \
  --measure-label "Total fixation duration (ms)" -o profile.html

Goal Where Save the figure or replay on screen Export → Current figure Export many trials and their tables Export → Export bundle Share a view or copy its code Share → Link or Code Reuse the design My designs, or Share → File

docs.title: Reproduce a figure
docs.text:
Open Share → Code and copy Python or CLI. The snippet carries the figure's settings and your column mapping; replace any placeholder file paths. Render in code shows a minimal example.

For a print-sized PNG, Python's save_figure accepts width_mm and dpi; the CLI uses --width-mm and --dpi. Use save_figure_layers or render --separable-layers for editable layers.

docs.title: Batch export
docs.text:
Export → Export bundle uses the chosen trials in the app. For a scripted batch, loop over the trial list:

Python: one HTML figure per trial 
from pathlib import Path

import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
out = Path("figures")
out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

for pid, tid in sps.list_trials(words, fixations).itertuples(index=False):
    fig = sps.plot_scanpath(words, fixations, pid, tid)
    sps.save_figure(fig, out / f"{pid}_{tid}.html")

Use the data loaders for your own files. The CLI's render writes one trial per invocation.

docs.title: Replay export
docs.text:
With Animate on, Export → Current figure saves HTML, GIF or MP4. The CLI's render --animate saves interactive HTML. For a GIF or MP4 in Python:

Python: save a GIF or MP4 
from pathlib import Path

import scanpath_studio as sps
from scanpath_studio.animation_export import export_animation

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
replay = sps.animate_scanpath(words, fixations, "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele_r0")
Path("replay.mp4").write_bytes(export_animation(replay, fmt="mp4"))

Use fmt="gif" and a .gif filename for GIF output.

docs.title: Data management
docs.text: Load your own data, open a public corpus, or try the bundled sample.

docs.title: Choose a dataset
docs.text:
Use the dataset picker or the Data Management page:

  • Bundled demo: a small OneStop sample
  • Hand-drawn sample: a six-word trial
  • Public corpora: OneStop and PoTeC, downloaded on your computer
    • → Import files: your own tables
    • → Create manually: type text and place fixations

docs.title: OneStop
docs.text: The demo comes from OneStop Eye Movements (Berzak et al., 2025), an English corpus with 360 participants. The full corpus is available as four datasets: ordinary reading, information seeking, and their repeated-reading versions. Each downloads once from OSF.

docs.title: What your data needs
docs.text:
At least one of the first three tables below; add others as needed.

Table Contents Fixations One row per fixation: trial ID, duration, and x/y or a word ID Words (interest areas) One row per word: trial ID, word ID and bounding box Raw gaze One row per sample: trial ID, x and y Participants One row per participant, with metadata Trials One row per trial, with metadata Texts One row per text, with metadata

Columns are detected from common eye-tracker exports; check and correct the mapping when importing. Keep condition labels and other columns with Extra fields to keep. Metadata fields are available for filtering, sorting and grouping.

docs.title: Files and units
docs.text:
• CSV, TSV, TXT, Parquet, Feather, Excel, or a ZIP of these files
  • Positions in pixels
  • Times in milliseconds; headers marked [s] or [μs] are converted
  • Word boxes as x/y/width/height or EyeLink's IA_LEFT/RIGHT/TOP/BOTTOM

docs.title: Trials over several screens
docs.text: Map screen_id in your tables, and screen_index for their order if needed. The app displays one screen at a time.

docs.title: Reading measures
docs.text: Include per-word reading measures in the Words table, such as first fixation duration or total fixation duration. EyeLink's IA_* columns are detected. Corpus Analysis uses the measures you supply.

docs.title: Add your own data
docs.text:
1. Choose + → Import files and name the dataset.
  2. Upload your tables and check the column mapping.
  3. Enter the recording screen size and typography where known.
  4. Optionally, on a local or desktop install, attach stimulus screenshots from a folder.
  5. Click Add dataset.

docs.title: Load and inspect in code
docs.text:
Load the same files in a script; column names are detected automatically.

scanpath-studio check --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv

For raw gaze, metadata and explicit column mappings, see the loaders and CLI input options.

docs.title: Manage datasets
docs.text:
Click a dataset row to open it. Inspect its tables, annotations and data checks below the list.

Use Edit dataset to change its name, column mapping, recording setup or metadata, then Save changes. Download setup file saves the mapping and recording setup for reuse.

Only imported columns are available in the editor. To use a column left out at import, add the files again.

docs.title: Scanpath visualization
docs.text:
1. Views and Help.
  2. The trial control bar: dataset, trial, screen, sort (⇅) and filter ().
  3. The trial's summary.
  4. The figure.
  5. Plot controls.
  6. Annotations, Stimulus & context, Comparisons, Export and Share.

The Scanpath view draws one reading on the screen it was recorded on.

Looking for a specific button?

All controls lists every button and setting on this view, menu by menu, with a picture of each menu. Search it for what you want to change, such as saccade color or legend position.

docs.title: Choose a trial
docs.text: Pick a trial above the plot. The filter () beside it narrows the list by text, participant, condition or annotation, and ⇅ sorts it. A trial with several screens gets a second navigator to move between them. When several participants have the same trial ID, each reading is in the list on its own, with its participant in brackets, 3 [p2].

docs.title: Control the layers
docs.text:
The Plot controls column holds every setting of the figure. Each layer is one line: a switch, and a ▾ with its settings.

Section What it controls Animate play the reading as a video, at a speed you choose Compare a second reading beside or over this one Design presets restyle the whole figure in one click: Scanpath, Heatmap, Illustration or your last custom settings My designs save the current settings as a design, apply it again in one click, or export it to share or use on another computer Palette one color scheme for the whole figure, such as colorblind-safe or print Fixations markers: size, color, order Saccades lines and arrows, colored by direction or reading type Stimulus text, span highlight, stimulus image, font and background Word boxes each word's interest area: outline and fill, color and opacity Heatmap where fixations concentrate, by count or duration Raw gaze the gaze samples as recorded Filters & highlights which fixations and saccades are drawn, and which stand out Figure & canvas screen framing, axes and grid, title and labels, hover fields, legends

docs.title: Under the plot
docs.text: Tab What it is for Annotations Star, tag and write notes on the trial, to find or filter it later. Stimulus & context The trial's context, such as its title, question and answers, and its highlighted word spans. Comparisons Compare this trial with other trials that match it on a field you choose, such as other readings of the same text, shown side by side. Export Download the figure (PNG, SVG, PDF, HTML) or the video (HTML, GIF, MP4), or a zip bundle of figures and data for many trials. Share A link that reopens this view (for whoever has the same dataset loaded), the Python or command-line code that redraws the figure, or a settings file. Watch the tabs under the figure

docs.title: Render in code
docs.text:
Set up a figure in the app, then open Share → Code for its Python or CLI recipe. For uploaded data, replace the placeholder file paths with your own.

Python and CLI: render the demo PythonCLI 
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(words, fixations, "l37_1129", "l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele_r0")
sps.save_figure(fig, "scanpath.html")

scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_1129 -t l37_1129_2_1_1_Ele_r0 -o scanpath.html

For your own files, use the data loaders. Figure settings are listed in the API options and CLI options.

The gallery gives app, CLI and Python instructions for heatmaps, comparisons, replays and other views. For batch exports and GIF/MP4, see Export and share.

docs.title: Back up your work
docs.text:
Each of these files can be saved and loaded again:

What Where figure settings Share → File favorites, tags and notes Data Management → Annotations → Export column mapping and recording setup Edit dataset → Download setup file saved figure designs My designs → Export

None of them holds your data, so load the same data before restoring one. On your own computer, the app also keeps your datasets and work between sessions.

docs.title: All controls
docs.text:
Every control on the Scanpath page, where it is and what it does — in the order you meet them on screen. Search this page (Ctrl+F, or Cmd+F on a Mac) for the thing you want to change, such as colors, legends or axes.

The page has two sets of controls:

  • The trial control bar, above the plot, decides what you see: the dataset, the trial, and which trials are in the list.
  • The plot controls, the column on the right, decide how it is drawn: each layer of the figure, its colors and sizes, and the figure as a whole.

The tabs under the plot then work with the trial on screen: annotate it, read its context, compare it, export it or share it. For how the parts fit together, see the Scanpath visualization guide.

For the corresponding Python keywords and CLI flags, use the figure options table.

docs.title: Trial control bar
docs.text:
The bar above the plot: pick a dataset and a trial, step through the trials, and narrow, sort or label the list.

Control What it does Select dataset The dataset the page shows. + → Create manually Add a dataset by manual illustration: write a text and place its fixations by hand. + → Import files Add a dataset from data tables: upload your own tables as a new dataset. Select trial The trial to show. Click it and type to narrow the list. Trial slider Scrub through the trials in the list. ◀ ▶ The previous or next trial. ⇅ → Sort trials by Reorder the trial list by a statistic (such as reading time), a participant, text or condition field, or a column of a metadata table you attached. ⇅ → Descending Reverse that order. → Text / Participant Keep only these texts or participants. → a field of your data Keep only trials with these values, or, for a number, in this range. → By participant / By trial / By text The same, for the columns of an attached metadata table. → Favorites only Keep only starred trials. → With any of these tags Keep only trials with any of these tags. → Excluding tags Hide trials with any of these tags, such as exclude. → Clear all filters Reset every filter in the panel. ✏️ → Show chips above the plot Show or hide the row of facts about the trial above the plot. ✏️ → field lists Drag fields between Shown and Available to choose the chips. Available holds every field with one value per trial: participant, text and condition columns, the columns of any metadata table you attached, and statistics such as reading time and fixation count. ✏️ → field colors Give a chip a highlight color; its ✕ puts it back to the default gray. ✏️ → Refresh fields Look again for which fields are trial-level. Screen and its ◀ ▶ On a trial recorded over several screens: the screen to show.

docs.title: Plot controls
docs.text: The column on the right of the plot. At the top, the modes and designs change the whole figure at once. Under them, each layer of the figure has a row of its own: the switch turns the layer on or off, and the ▾ beside it opens that layer's settings, described below one menu at a time. The last two rows, Filters & highlights and Figure & canvas, cover the figure as a whole. A greyed-out control says why when you hover over it.

docs.title: Animate: play the reading as a video
docs.text:
The Animate switch turns the figure into an animation, a video of the reading played back fixation by fixation, with play and pause buttons and a time slider under the plot. Its ▾ holds:

Control What it does Replay → Speed How fast the video plays, from ×0.25 to ×8: ×1 is the reader's own pace, ×2 twice as fast, ×0.5 half as fast. Replay → Autoplay → On load Start playing the animation automatically as soon as the plot is shown; otherwise it starts only when you click play. Replay → Duration For information only: the trial's reading time, and how long the video runs at this speed. Frames → Quality How smooth the video is: more frames play more smoothly but take longer to build. Custom sets the two below by hand. Frames → Every Reading time between frames, in ms. Frames → Limit The most frames a video gets; a long trial gets wider frame steps to fit. Frames → Result For information only: how many frames this trial's video has, and how far apart they ended up.

docs.title: Compare
docs.text:
The Compare switch shows a second scanpath, B, beside or over this one (pick it in the trial control bar, above the plot); its ▾ holds:

Control What it does View Overlay both scanpaths, or give each its own panel, Side by side or Top & bottom. Stimulus from In an overlay, whose word boxes and text are drawn: both, A's or B's. Label A / Label B Each scanpath's name in the legend, written with fields such as {participant_id}; empty uses the automatic one. Available fields The fields a label can use. Step → A and B together ◀ ▶ move both scanpaths at once.

docs.title: Design presets and palette
docs.text:
Restyle the whole figure in one click, with a ready-made design or one of your own saved designs:

Control What it does Scanpath / Heatmap / Illustration Ready-made designs: a classic scanpath, a word-box heatmap, or a clean schematic. Custom Your most recent hand-made settings. My designs Your saved designs: click one to apply it; the pencil renames it and the bin deletes it. My designs → save button Save the settings on screen as a named design, to apply again later in one click. My designs → Export / Import Download your designs as a file, or load a file of designs: share a look with co-authors and partners, reproduce a figure exactly, or move your designs to another computer. Palette A color scheme for the whole figure, such as colorblind-safe or print.

docs.title: Fixations
docs.text:
The Fixations switch draws the fixation markers; its ▾ holds:

Control What it does Marker → Color What decides each marker's color. One color paints them all alike. Pick a number column of the fixations, such as duration or the fixation's order in the trial, and the markers follow a color scale: with the default blues, longer fixations show darker. Pick a category, such as the line of text or the next saccade's direction, and each value gets its own color, with a legend. Marker → color box Choose the fixation marker color. Marker → Range When markers are colored by a number: the values at the two ends of the color scale. Auto fits each trial. Marker → Shape Choose the fixation marker shape: circle, square, diamond, triangle, star… Marker → Size Set the marker size range: the smallest and largest marker diameter, in px. Marker → Scale Choose how duration sets marker size: square root, linear, log, or relative to the figure (its shortest to its longest fixation). Marker → Durations Choose the duration range: set the durations that get the smallest and the largest marker. Marker → Opacity Set the fixation marker opacity; lower it to see overlapping fixations. Marker → Outline Set the width and color of the ring round each marker. Color bar → Show Show the color scale's bar, when markers are colored by a number. Color bar → orientation, Angle, Size, Thickness, Length Set the bar's direction, tick-label angle and size, and its thickness and length. Fixation index → Show Number each fixation in reading order. Fixation index → color, Size Choose the numbers' color and size. Snap → To line Move each fixation onto its line of text — a schematic, labelled Illustration. Snap → Position Choose where on its line a snapped fixation sits.

docs.title: Saccades
docs.text:
The Saccades switch draws the lines between fixations; its ▾ holds:

Control What it does Line → Color Choose what decides the saccade color: one color for all; forward saccades and regressions in two colors; or a color per saccade type (forward, skip, refixation, return sweep, regression), with a legend. Forward / regression and by type need a word ID for each fixation, the word it landed on, mapped in your fixations table (such as EyeLink's CURRENT_FIX_INTEREST_AREA_ID); without one every saccade reads as other. Line → color box Choose the saccade line color. Line → type colors With By type: choose the color of each saccade type, such as regressions or return sweeps. Line → Style Choose the saccade line style: solid, dashed, dotted or dash-dot. Line → Width Set the saccade line width (thickness), in px. Line → Opacity Set the saccade line and arrow opacity; lower it to bring the fixations forward. Shape Choose the saccade shape: straight lines, or arcs over the text (a schematic, labelled Illustration). Direction arrows → Show Show saccade direction arrows: an arrowhead on each saccade, pointing where the eye went. Direction arrows → Arrow size Set the saccade arrowhead size.

docs.title: Stimulus
docs.text:
The Stimulus switch draws the text and the stimulus image; its ▾ holds:

Control What it does Text → Show Show the stimulus text, the words the participant read, at their place on the screen. Fit → Fit to word boxes Size the stimulus text to fill its word boxes, instead of a fixed font size. Spacing Set the stimulus text line spacing: how far apart the lines are, in font sizes. Size Set the stimulus text font size, in px or pt. Font Choose the stimulus text font (typeface); Other… takes any font name. Color → text color Choose the stimulus text color. Background Choose the plot background color: a preset, or any color in the box beside it. Highlight → Show Highlight words in the stimulus text, such as the answer span. Highlight → Highlight words by Choose which words to highlight: a true/false word column, such as the critical span. Style Choose the word highlight style: colored text, or a border round the words; and the highlight color. Image → Show Show the stimulus image, the screen as shown in the experiment, under the scanpath. File Upload a stimulus image (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP) to draw under the scanpath. Opacity Set the stimulus image opacity; lower it so the scanpath reads over it. Offset → X / Y Move (nudge) the stimulus image left, right, up or down, in px, to line it up with the word boxes. Scale Resize (scale) the stimulus image so its text matches the word boxes.

docs.title: Word boxes
docs.text:
The Word boxes switch draws each word's interest area; its ▾ holds:

Control What it does Box → Line color Choose the word box outline (border) color. Box → Line opacity Set the word box outline opacity; 0 hides the outlines. Box → Fill color Choose the word box fill color, inside each box. Box → Fill opacity Set the word box fill opacity; 0 draws outlines only.

docs.title: Heatmap
docs.text:
The Heatmap switch shows where reading concentrated; its ▾ holds:

Control What it does Style Choose the heatmap style: colored word boxes, or a smooth interpolated map. Blur Set the heatmap blur: how far each fixation spreads, for the interpolated style; Auto picks it. Color → By Choose what the heatmap measures: total fixation duration (dwell time), or the number of fixations. Color → Colors Choose the heatmap colors (color scale). Scale Choose a linear or log heatmap scale. Range For word-box heatmaps, fix the color range across trials. Auto fits each trial. Interpolated heatmaps use each figure's own peak. Opacity Set the heatmap opacity; Auto uses each style's own. Color bar → Show, orientation, Angle, Size, Thickness, Length Show the heatmap color bar, and set its orientation, label angle and size, thickness and length.

docs.title: Raw gaze
docs.text:
The Raw gaze switch draws the gaze samples as recorded; its ▾ holds:

Control What it does Marker → Color Not used outside Compare: the samples are colored by their time, or by their order when they have no timestamps. Marker → Size Set the raw gaze sample marker size. Marker → Opacity Set the raw gaze sample opacity.

docs.title: Filters & highlights
docs.text:
Which fixations and saccades are drawn, and which stand out:

Control What it does Fixations → Index range Show only some fixations: a range of the reading order, such as fixations 10 to 40. Fixations → All trials Keep that fixation range when you move to another trial; otherwise it applies to this trial only, and the next trial shows all its fixations. Short / Long Find short or long fixations by a duration threshold (ms): Highlight marks them, Discard hides them. Out of bounds Highlight or discard out-of-bounds fixations, which land in no word box. Blink Highlight or discard fixations at or next to a blink (needs a blink column). marker and color Choose the marker shape and color of each highlighted fixation kind. Saccades → Types Show only some saccade types, such as regressions or return sweeps. Needs a word ID for each fixation, as for coloring saccades by type.

docs.title: Figure & canvas
docs.text:
The figure as a whole:

Control What it does Frame → Crop to data Crop (zoom) the figure to the part of the screen with data, instead of the whole screen. Margin Set the crop margin: the space round the data when cropping; Auto uses 5%. Border → Show, color Show the border line round the plot area, and choose its color. It marks the edge of the screen, or, with Crop to data, the edge of the cropped area. Grid → Show Show pixel grid lines (a coordinate grid) over the screen. Grid → Auto, interval Set the grid spacing (interval), in px, or let Auto choose it. Labels Set the grid label (tick label) font size. Axes → X / Y Choose the x and y axis fields. X / Y draws the reading on the screen. Any other pair turns the figure into a scatter plot (chart) of the fixations, with no text, word boxes or saccades, keeping the marker colors and sizes. For example: Time (ms) against X for a time course of the reading, where regressions show as dips; Time (ms) against Word # for reading progress through the text; Fixation # against Duration (ms) for fixation durations over the trial. Illustration → Label Choose when to label the figure as a manual illustration, not the recorded positions: when a setting changes its geometry (such as snapping fixations to a line or drawing saccades as arcs), always, or never. Illustration → Text Write the Illustration label's text. Title → Show, text, Size Add a figure title above the plot, and set its font size; {field} inserts a value of the trial. Caption → Show, text, Size, color Add a figure caption below the plot, and set its font size and color. Hover → Words / Fixations Choose the hover fields: what the tooltip shows when the mouse is over a word or a fixation. Legends → Show Show or hide each legend: Compare (A/B), Saccade types, Fixation colors, Size key or Text highlight. Legends → Position Choose the legend position: a corner, the middle of an edge, or down a side, outside or inside the plot. Legends → Arrangement Choose the legend arrangement: items stacked or side by side. Legends → Text size Set the legend text (font) size, in px.

docs.title: Reset visualization
docs.text:
The button at the foot of the column.

Control What it does Reset visualization Reset all plot settings to the defaults. Annotations, filters, data and the selected trial stay.

docs.title: In Compare
docs.text:
With Compare on, scanpath B gets a row of its own, and several menus split into a Scanpath A and a Scanpath B group.

Control What it does Dataset B Choose the dataset scanpath B comes from: this one, or another dataset. Trial B, slider, ◀ ▶ Choose scanpath B's trial: 📄 marks the same text, 👤 the same participant. ⇅ on B's row Sort scanpath B's trial list, apart from A's. By default, trials of the same text as A come first, then the same participant, then the rest; or sort by any field, as on A's row. on B's row Filter scanpath B's trials, apart from A's. Fixations ▾ → Scanpath A / B → Color, Size, Opacity Choose each scanpath's fixation marker color, size range and opacity. Saccades ▾ → Scanpath A / B → Color, Style, Width Choose each scanpath's saccade line color, style and width. Word boxes ▾ → Scanpath A / B → Line, Fill Choose each scanpath's word box outline and fill colors and opacities. Heatmap ▾ → Scanpath A / B → Colors Choose each scanpath's heatmap colors (color scale). Raw gaze ▾ → Scanpath A / B → Color Choose each scanpath's raw gaze sample color. Filters & highlights ▾ → · B groups Set scanpath B's own fixation range, fixation highlights and saccade types.

docs.title: Under the plot
docs.text:
The tabs under the figure:

Tab Control What it does Annotations Favorite Star the trial as a favorite, to find it again with the favorites filter. Tags / Add a tag Tag the trial, with an existing tag or a new one, such as exclude. Tags let you filter the trial list later: the in the trial control bar keeps or hides trials by tag. Notes Write a free-text note on the trial. Stimulus & context Context fields Choose the trial context to show, such as the text's title, a question or an answer. Highlighted spans Choose true/false word columns to highlight in the text, each with a summary. Comparisons Match field Compare with other trials: show the trials that share this trial's value of a field, such as the same text. Columns Set how many comparison panels per row. Export Download format Export (download) the figure on screen as PNG, SVG, PDF or HTML, or the animation as an HTML, GIF or MP4 video. Width, unit, DPI Set the PNG export size for print: width, unit and resolution (DPI). Trials to include Choose which trials to export in the bundle: this one, the filtered trials, or all of them. Formats / Tabular data Choose the bundle's figure formats and the data tables (CSV or Parquet) to include. Separable layers Export each visual layer (fixations, saccades, word boxes…) as its own file, to stack in a vector editor. Annotations (JSON) / Settings file (JSON) Settings file: beside each trial's figure, a plot_config.json recording how it was drawn (layers, colors, sizes, screen, title and caption), so the figures are documented. Annotations: one annotations.json with the exported trials' favorites, tags and notes, which Data Management → Annotations can import again. File path pattern Set the file names inside the export bundle. Build export Build the export bundle (a zip) to download. Share Link Copy a share link that reopens this trial with these settings. The data doesn't travel in the link: whoever opens it needs the same dataset. The bundled demo works anywhere; a public corpus has to be downloaded on their side; for your own dataset, send its files and setup file ( Edit dataset → Download setup file) so they can add it first. A link made on your own computer (a localhost address) opens only where the app runs at that same address. Code → Flavour, Show every option Get the Python or command-line code that redraws this figure, for scripts and reproduction. File → Download settings / Restore settings Save the plot settings to a file, or load (restore) a saved settings file.

docs.text:
Choose a task. For installation, see Get started; for control reference, see the feature guides.

  • Optimize data collection

    • Check a session

  • Filter data

    • Exclude unsuitable trials
    • Select participants by a field

  • Export customized figures

    • Export one figure

  • Analyze a corpus

    • Analyze one text

In the app, open Help → Tutorials for guided tours of the controls.

docs.title: Analyze a corpus
docs.text:
• Analyze one text

    Compare word-by-word measures across readers.

  • Compare groups or conditions

    Inspect group means and differences.

  • See progression over time

    Inspect trends within or across trials.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Open a dataset and set the trial filters for your question. Word-level views need reading measures in the Words table; the bundled demo includes them. For comparisons across readers, the same text must have the same text ID.

docs.title: Keep the result
docs.text:
Download this table (CSV) saves the values. Download the recipe (JSON) saves the dataset name, filters, analysis choices and counts. Keep the source data separately so the result can be reproduced.

To draw a summary with Python or the CLI, see Plot a summary in code.

docs.title: Analyze one text
docs.text:
Compare how participants read the words of one text.

  1. Select the trials, then open Corpus Analysis → Per text.
  2. Pick a text and an available reading measure.
  3. Choose a word profile on the stimulus or a plot against a word feature, such as surprisal if that column is present.
  4. Set the aggregation, spread and minimum participants per word. Check the counts before interpreting differences.
  5. Download the table and recipe.

The recording shows total fixation duration on a text, against GPT-2 surprisal, and between two groups.

docs.title: Compare groups or conditions
docs.text:
Compare a reading measure between two cohorts.

  1. Select the trials, then open Corpus Analysis → Groups.
  2. Turn on Compare a second group.
  3. Split a field or define independent filters for the two groups.
  4. Choose Group means & difference and a measure. Check the number of participants in each group and any overlap. A standardized difference is shown only for non-overlapping groups.
  5. Download the table and recipe.

The comparison is descriptive; it does not run a significance test. For a recorded example, see Analyze one text.

docs.title: See progression over time
docs.text:
Inspect a measure within trials or across a session.

  1. Select the trials and open Corpus Analysis.

  2. Choose the view for the question:

    Scope View One participant across trials Per participant → Per-trial trend Fixation duration within trials, pooled for one participant Per participant → Fixation duration over time A group across trials Groups → Group trend

  3. Choose a measure and aggregation where offered. For across-trial trends, map the recorded trial-order column when importing; inferred order may differ from presentation order. For the within-trial view, choose fixation order or recorded onset time if available.

  4. Download the table and recipe.

docs.title: Optimize data collection
docs.text:
• Check a session

    Inspect a pilot or completed recording.

  • Compare two eye trackers

    Review recordings of the same text.

  • Audit an experimenter

    Review sessions by who collected them.

Start with a loaded dataset. To apply exclusion decisions after reviewing, use Filter data.

docs.title: Audit an experimenter
docs.text:
Review recordings collected by one experimenter.

  1. Keep an experimenter field when importing the data, or attach it in a participants table if each participant has one experimenter.
  2. Open the filter button beside Select trial and choose the experimenter. Participants-table fields appear under By participant.
  3. Inspect and replay their trials.
  4. Tag trials review in Annotations and note recurring observations.
  5. Export the review.

To compare experimenters, turn on Compare, filter each scanpath's trial list by a different experimenter, and select readings of the same text.

docs.title: Check a session
docs.text: Inspect a recording and save the trials that need attention.

docs.title: 1. Open the session
docs.text: Import your tables, or select a loaded dataset. Check its Recording setup against the screen used in the experiment.

docs.title: 2. Inspect a trial
docs.text:
Select a participant and trial in Scanpath. Turn on Word boxes and inspect:

  • whether the boxes match the stimulus screenshot, if available;
  • how fixations sit relative to the words;
  • unexpected gaps, shifts or off-screen positions.

For a consistent offset, check coordinate units and screen setup.

docs.title: 3. Replay the recording
docs.text: Turn on Animate to inspect fixation order and timing. To mark short, long or out-of-bounds fixations, use Plot controls → Filters & highlights → Fixations and choose Highlight. Gaps and unusual scanpaths alone do not establish their cause.

docs.title: 4. Record the review
docs.text: In Annotations, tag a trial review and note what you observed. Use the trial picker's arrows to continue through the session.

docs.title: 5. Save the review
docs.text:
Export stars, tags and notes from Data Management → Annotations → Export. The record includes participant and trial IDs. Use Open on an annotation row to return to that trial.

For exclusion decisions, follow Exclude unsuitable trials.

docs.title: Compare two eye trackers
docs.text:
Review the same text recorded with two trackers or setups.

  1. Import each recording as a separate dataset with its own Recording setup.
  2. Open the first dataset and select a trial in Scanpath.
  3. Turn on Compare. In scanpath B's row, choose Dataset B and a trial of the same text.
  4. Compare fixation placement, spread and missing stretches. Use side-by-side views for different screen sizes; an overlay requires matching screen coordinates.

This recording compares two readers in the demo. For two trackers, select the second recording under Dataset B.

Use the session-review steps to save observations.

docs.title: Filter data
docs.text:
• Exclude unsuitable trials

    Leave tagged trials out.

  • Select participants by a field

    Use participant metadata.

  • Find the trials an analysis needs

    Select trials after inspecting fixations.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Open a dataset in Scanpath. The filter button beside Select trial selects whole trials. Plot controls → Filters & highlights changes which fixations and saccades the figure draws.

docs.title: Check and export the selection
docs.text:
1. Check the remaining trial and participant counts and inspect a few trials.
  2. Follow Export every trial, choosing the active filtered pool. The bundle's index.csv lists its files and trial IDs.
  3. Keep a full decision record with Data Management → Annotations → Export. Bundle annotations cover only the exported trials.

docs.title: Exclude unsuitable trials
docs.text:
Apply your exclusion criteria and leave rejected trials out of the selection.

  1. Review the session. Judge trials against your study's criteria; a scanpath pattern alone does not establish skimming or poor calibration.
  2. In Annotations, tag rejected trials exclude and add a brief reason.
  3. Open the filter button beside Select trial. Under By trial annotation, choose exclude in Excluding tags.
  4. Check and export the selection.

For trials with several screens, apply the exclusion tag to the whole trial. A screen-only annotation does not exclude its parent trial.

The recording shows stars and tags. Use the exclude tag and Excluding tags for the selection above.

docs.title: Find the trials an analysis needs
docs.text:
Locate trials containing particular fixation patterns.

  1. Open Plot controls → Filters & highlights → Fixations.

  2. Set the relevant category to Highlight:

    • Short or Long, with a duration threshold in milliseconds
    • Out of bounds, for fixations outside every word box
    • Blink, if your data includes a blink column

  3. Step through the trials. In Annotations, tag those that meet your analysis criteria, for example include.

  4. Open the filter button beside Select trial. Under By trial annotation, choose include in With any of these tags.
  5. Check and export the selection.

docs.title: Select participants by a field
docs.text:
Select readers using metadata such as native language, age or group.

  1. Attach a table with one row per participant and a participant ID column: use Metadata → Participants when adding a dataset, or Data Management → Edit dataset → Data tables & column mapping afterwards.
  2. Open the filter button beside Select trial, then By participant.
  3. Choose a field and the values or range to keep.
  4. Check the remaining participant IDs and export the selection.

To also apply trial-level quality criteria, follow Exclude unsuitable trials.

docs.title: Export customized figures
docs.text:
• Export one figure

    A static image or interactive HTML.

  • Export a replay

    GIF, MP4 or interactive HTML.

  • Export every trial

    A ZIP of figures and data tables.

For installation requirements or a failed export, see the export FAQ.

docs.title: Export a replay
docs.text:
Save an animated reading for a talk or supplement.

  1. Select a trial in Scanpath and turn on Animate.
  2. Set the playback speed and visible layers.
  3. Open Export → Current figure and choose GIF, MP4 or HTML.
  4. Download the replay. GIF and MP4 use the selected playback speed; HTML has interactive playback controls.

Exporting a GIF; the rendering wait is shortened in this recording.

For GIF/MP4 export from Python, see Export and share.

docs.title: Export every trial
docs.text:
Build a ZIP of static figures and data tables for a set of trials.

  1. Set the figure's design once. Each exported trial uses that design, without animation or a comparison partner.
  2. Open Export → Export bundle and select this trial, the active filtered pool, or the whole dataset.
  3. Choose figure and table formats and check the filename pattern. For editing individual layers later, enable separable layers.
  4. Build and download the bundle, then inspect one exported figure.

Exporting figures and tables for the demo's trials; the build is fast-forwarded.
